jobDescription: The regional distribution team runs four warehouses that ship household goods to retail stores and online customers. The Fulfilment Operations Analyst owns the weekly dispatch reporting, runs late-order reviews with the warehouse supervisors, maintains the dispatch-scheduling rules in the warehouse management system and prepares the monthly operations pack. The team expects improvement claims to be shown against a documented baseline before they are reported upward.
requirements: Builds and maintains the weekly dispatch performance report across the regional warehouses.
Runs root-cause reviews of late orders with the warehouse supervisors and tracks the resulting actions.
Maintains the slotting and dispatch-scheduling rules in the warehouse management system through the change process.
Demonstrates a measured improvement in order-to-dispatch time against a documented baseline and measurement window.
Prepares the monthly operations pack for the regional operations manager.

evidence.text: Built the weekly dispatch performance report for four regional warehouses in the warehouse management system's reporting module, covering order volumes, pick rates and late orders by carrier.
Ran fortnightly late-order reviews with the warehouse supervisors, logging each root cause (stock-outs, missed carrier cut-offs, picking errors) in a shared tracker and chasing the open actions.
Cut average order-to-dispatch time by 27% across the regional network after redesigning the dispatch-scheduling rules.
Maintained the slotting and dispatch-scheduling rules in the warehouse management system, submitting each change through the systems team's change log for approval.
Assembled the monthly operations pack (volumes, service levels, open late-order actions) for the regional operations manager over two years.

Work sample: an anonymised weekly dispatch report for one warehouse, with order volumes, pick rates, late orders by carrier and the late-order action tracker for that week; it shows a single week and contains no comparison of dispatch times across periods.
HR verification note: employment dates (March 2022 to May 2024) and the job title Fulfilment Operations Analyst were checked against the employment letter the candidate supplied and match it.
Recruiter logistics note: candidate is available for a second-round interview on Tuesday or Thursday and has asked for the site visit to include the regional dispatch office.

propositions.text: The candidate built the weekly dispatch performance report for four regional warehouses, covering order volumes, pick rates and late orders by carrier.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the report and the work sample shows one week of it.

propositions.text: The candidate ran fortnightly late-order root-cause reviews with the warehouse supervisors and tracked the resulting actions.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the reviews and the work sample includes the action tracker.

propositions.text: The candidate reduced average order-to-dispatch time by 27% across the regional network.
propositions.rationale: The 27% figure is the candidate's own statement with no baseline, measurement window or report, and the work sample contains no cross-period comparison; under the quantification rule a figure without a defined baseline is not evidence.

gold.expectedGap: No baseline, measurement window or report supports the stated reduction in order-to-dispatch time.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: The packet reports the documented reporting, review and rule-maintenance work; the stated dispatch-time reduction is recorded as an unsupported claim until a baseline and measurement window are provided.
followUpTargets: Ask for the order-to-dispatch baseline, the measurement window and the report that compares the periods before and after the rule change.
